Chernivtsi Sadhora Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernivetska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Chernivtsi's Sadhora district holds one of the most significant sites in this entire collection: this cemetery was vandalized during WWI, and among the destroyed burials were the gravestones of the famous Rabbi Israel Friedman of Ruzhin — founder of the Ruzhin Hasidic dynasty, documented at his original seat elsewhere in this collection — along with two of his sons, Avraham Yaakov of Sadigura and Dov Ber of Leova, and other family members. These graves were replaced afterward by a large white concrete slab, and their ohel was renovated in the 2010s by the Ohalei Tzaddikim foundation, documented at several other sites in this collection. In the 1840s, Rabbi Israel Friedman set up a Hasidic court in Sadhora after fleeing his original seat, building a synagogue that accommodated 1,000 worshippers; Sadhora became a famous site of pilgrimage in the Hasidic world, and the Jewish population reached 80.4 percent of the town by 1880. When WWI began, his son Avraham Yakov Friedman, then head of the Hasidic court, escaped to Vienna and established his court there, though he was evidently later buried back in Sadhora. Jews were among the town's founders in 1770.
